raw_snippet: 6.1 million workers (4.2% of the workforce in our sample) work in occupations that are both highly exposed and where workers have low expected adaptive capacity
note: Manning & Aguirre, NBER Working Paper 34705 (January 2026). Corrected 22 Sep 2026: this row read 3.3 million (2.5 percent), from the NBER chapter page, which carries an earlier draft; the working paper's abstract, the later text, states 6.1 million (4.2 percent) of the 356-occupation sample, with 37.1 million in the top exposure quartile of whom 26.5 million have above-median adaptive capacity. The old row stays in the ledger, superseded. No independent second source found (Brookings/GovAI pages are the authors').
